tests.name: Laboratory Accuracy Tests
tests.description: Tests intended for verifying compliance of the design and construction of a particular type or model of IR thermometer with the error limitations specified in 5.3 or 5.4, or both.

tests.name: Blackbody Test
tests.description: Under laboratory conditions, an IR thermometer shall be tested against a blackbody standard. The true temperature of the blackbody shall be monitored by a contact imbedded or immersed thermometer with uncertainty no greater than ±0.03 °C (±0.05 °F).

tests.name: Ear Canal Type IR Thermometer Test
tests.description: Tests repeated for three blackbody temperatures (35, 37, 41 °C) within ±0.5 °C. At least six measurements per blackbody temperature per ambient condition combination.

tests.name: Skin Type IR Thermometer Test
tests.description: Testing as specified in 6.1.4 except blackbody temperatures set within ±1 °C (±2 °F) from 23, 30, and 38 °C (73, 86, and 100 °F). Greatest calculated error δj shall conform with requirements in 5.4.

tests.name: Storage Test
tests.description: IR thermometer maintained at –20 °C (<50% RH) for 30 days and at 50 °C (≥75% RH noncondensing) for 30 days. After each exposure, tested per 6.3.2 and 6.3.3.

tests.name: Clinical Accuracy Tests
tests.description: Manufacturers shall perform clinical accuracy testing in accordance with methods acceptable to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

tests.name: Clinical Accuracy Tests - Purpose
tests.description: Evaluation of accuracy of built-in instrumentational or combined site offsets, and performance of an IR thermometer in assessing internal body temperatures from actual subjects.

tests.name: Clinical Accuracy Tests - Reference Sites
tests.description: Tests performed on groups of subjects using an internal body site (e.g., pulmonary artery or sublingual cavity) for reference measurements.

tests.name: Shock Test - Drop Test Procedure
tests.description: IR thermometer subjected to fall from 1 m onto 50 mm thick hardwood board (density >700 kg/m3) on rigid base. Two axes tested: Axis A (optical axis of probe), Axis B (through center of gravity and probe window crossing point). Probe faces down.

tests.name: Shock Test - Post-Drop Measurement Verification
tests.description: Measure blackbody set within ±0.5°C (±1°F) from 37°C (98.6°F), ambient 20-26°C (68-79°F), RH 40-70%. At least 5 measurements with new disposable probe cover per measurement. Unadjusted mode per 5.8.2.2.

tests.name: Shock Test - Error Evaluation
tests.description: Unadjusted temperature value subtracted from blackbody setting. Absolute value of largest error shall be no greater than error limit in 5.3 or 5.4 for blackbody temperature range 36-39°C (96.8-102.2°F).

tests.name: EMC - RF Field Exposure
tests.description: Instrument exposed to modulated electromagnetic RF field per IEC601-1-2 and IEC 1000-4-3.

tests.name: EMC - Field Strength
tests.description: 3 V/m

tests.name: EMC - Carrier Frequency Range
tests.description: 26 MHz to 1 GHz

tests.name: EMC - Frequency Sweep Interval
tests.description: 1 MHz/s minimum

tests.name: EMC - Frequency Interval Dwell Time
tests.description: Greater of 1 s or measurement response time of instrument under test

tests.name: EMC - AM Modulation
tests.description: 80% index with sine wave or 100% with square wave (50% duty cycle). Modulation frequency within each significant signal-processing passband. For devices without defined passband: 1 Hz, 10 Hz, and 1 kHz.

tests.name: EMC - Probe Cover Change
tests.description: No change of probe covers required during electromagnetic compatibility test.

tests.name: EMC - Target Condition
tests.description: IR thermometer probe aimed at target whose surface temperature is within display range. Target does not have to be a blackbody.

tests.name: EMC - Continuous Reading Devices
tests.description: IR thermometers capable of continuous temperature readings shall have readings taken successively and compared during frequency sweep interval.

tests.name: EMC - Non-Continuous Reading Devices
tests.description: Circuitry modified to allow continuous monitoring of IR and reference temperature signals. Peak excursions recalculated to represent temperature excursions.

tests.name: EMC - Digital Output Devices
tests.description: Signal monitored at output of analog-to-digital converter.

tests.name: EMC - Connection Type
tests.description: Non-conductive and dielectric connections (e.g., fiber-optic) used between IR thermometer and test equipment to minimize perturbations of electromagnetic field.

tests.name: EMC - Temperature Excursion Deviation
tests.description: Calculated temperature excursions shall deviate from one another by value no greater than required by 5.6.6.

tests.name: ESD Test - General
tests.description: Effects of electrostatic discharge on accuracy tested per IEC 1000-4-2:1995.

tests.name: ESD Test - Power State
tests.description: IR thermometer shall be in 'power on' state when subjected to electrostatic discharge.

tests.name: ESD Test - Number of Discharges
tests.description: Ten air and ten contact discharges shall be applied.

tests.name: ESD Test - No Exposed Conductive Parts
tests.description: If no exposed electrically conductive parts, only air discharge shall be applied.

tests.name: ESD - Air Discharge Target
tests.description: Discharge aimed at electrically nonconductive part of IR thermometer probe with no probe cover attached.

tests.name: ESD - Air Discharge Level
tests.description: Discharge levels: 2 kV, 4 kV, and 8 kV.
Electrostatic discharge test

Conditions of acceptability: 1) 5.5.1 Clinical Accuracy is not evaluated in this report. 2) 5.9.1 Housing Materials is not evaluated in this report. 3) 6.2 Clinical Accuracy Tests is not evaluated in this report.

General remarks: '(see Attachment #)' refers to additional information appended to the report. '(see appended table)' refers to a table appended to the report. The tests results presented in this report relate only to the object tested. This report shall not be reproduced except in full without the written approval of the testing laboratory. List of test equipment must be kept on file and available for review. This Test Report Form is intended for the investigation of clinical thermometers for body temperature measurement in accordance with ASTM E 1965-98(2023). Additional test data and/or information provided in the attachments to this report. Throughout this report a comma/point is used as the decimal separator.

General disclaimer: The test results presented in this report relate only to the object tested. Without permission of the Report department this test report is not permitted to be duplicated in extracts.
Copy of marking plate: The artwork below may be only a draft. The use of certification marks on a product must be authorized by the respective NCBs that own these marks.

Clinical accuracy is not evaluated in this report. The clinical accuracy requirement is applicable only to an ear canal IR thermometer system and the corresponding age groups of subjects for which such a thermometer is labeled or implied to be used. Clinical accuracy shall be determined separately for each device model, for each adjusted display mode, and for every age group of febrile and afebrile subjects on which the IR thermometer is intended to be used.

If the operating temperature range is narrower than 16 to 40 °C (60.8 to 104.0 °F) as specified in 5.6.1.1, the device shall be clearly labeled with a cautionary statement of the maximum or minimum operating temperatures, or both. The product's operating temperature is 10℃-40℃, which is narrower than 16-40°C at the lower end, making this clause applicable.

Storage Conditions: The instrument shall meet the accuracy requirements of 5.3 or 5.4, or both, after having been stored or transported, or both, at any point in an environment of -20 to +50 °C (-4 to +122 °F) and relative humidity up to 95%, noncondensing, for a period of one month. The test procedure is specified in 6.1.6. Result: See TABLE 5.6.4. Verdict: P.

An IR thermometer that is intended for professional use shall meet the accuracy requirements of 5.3 or 5.4, or both, for temperature ranges of 6.3.2, during and after exposure to electromagnetic interference. This requirement is not applicable as the device is not intended for professional use.

Labeling requirement 5.10.1.3: An IR thermometer intended for professional use shall be conspicuously labelled with an indication of the unadjusted or adjusted mode(s). Such labeling is optional for IR thermometers that display only one mode and are intended for non-professional use. However, the instruction manual for both professional and non-professional use IR thermometers shall specify the body site(s) used to reference the adjusted temperature value(s) displayed. This clause is N/A as the device is for non-professional use.

Housing Materials requirement (5.9.1): All materials that may come in contact with the operator or a subject shall be nontoxic. Compliance evidence referenced to Biocompatibility test report provided by manufacturer. Result marked N/E (Not Evaluated in this report).

Warning Signs specification (5.8.3): The instrument shall have means to inform the operator when the following are outside the operating ranges specified by the manufacturer: power supply, subject temperature, and ambient temperature. Implementation: Low power supply warning threshold is 2.7V; outside the operating temperature range and ambient temperature are indicated by displaying '---'.

For Skin Type IR Thermometer testing (6.1.5), blackbody temperatures shall be set within ±1 °C (±2 °F) from 23 °C, 30 °C, and 38 °C (73, 86, and 100 °F). Testing procedure follows 6.1.4 requirements: stabilization for minimum 30 min, at least six measurements per blackbody temperature per ambient condition combination, new disposable probe cover for each test reading if applicable. Three data sets formed per mode; greatest calculated error δj shall conform with requirements in 5.4.

Storage Test (6.1.6): An IR thermometer shall be maintained in an environmental chamber at –20 °C (–4 °F), relative humidity below 50%, for 30 days; and at 50 °C (122 °F), relative humidity no less than 75% noncondensing, for 30 days. After each exposure, the IR thermometer shall be tested according to 6.3.2 and 6.3.3.

Sampling Plans (6.1): Tests are not required for every produced instrument. Each producer or distributor representing its instruments as conforming to this specification shall utilize statistically based sampling plans appropriate for each particular manufacturing process, in the design qualification of the device, and shall keep essential records to document with a high degree of assurance that all requirements are met. The manufacturer shall make sampling plans available upon request.

Clinical Accuracy Tests (6.2): This specification does not prescribe an actual method for determining clinical accuracy or establish specifications for values which characterize clinical accuracy. Manufacturers shall perform clinical accuracy testing in accordance with methods acceptable to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. An example method is provided in X2.3.

Blackbody Test (6.1.3): Under laboratory conditions, an IR thermometer shall be tested against a blackbody standard. A recommended blackbody design is provided in Annex A1. The temperature of the blackbody shall be measured by the IR thermometer being tested in accordance with a procedure recommended by the manufacturer. The true temperature of the blackbody shall be monitored by a contact imbedded or immersed thermometer with uncertainty no greater than ±0.03 °C (±0.05 °F). A manufacturer may require testing only with a manufacturer-specified blackbody rather than that described in Annex A1.

Clinical accuracy tests are intended for evaluation of accuracy of built-in instrumentational or combined site offsets, or both, and performance of an IR thermometer in assessing internal body temperatures from actual subjects. While this specification does not set limits for clinical accuracy, it is the responsibility of a manufacturer to determine values characterizing clinical accuracy and disclose them upon request.

Shock Test Procedure (6.3.1): IR thermometer subjected to fall from 1 m onto 50 mm thick hardwood board (density >700 kg/m3) on rigid base (concrete block). Controlled orientation: once for each of two axes where probe faces down. Axis A = optical axis of probe; Axis B = passes through center of gravity and point where probe window crosses Axis A.

Post-shock measurement verification (6.3.2): Measure blackbody set within ±0.5°C (±1°F) from 37°C (98.6°F). Ambient conditions: 20-26°C (68-79°F), RH 40-70%. Minimum 5 measurements with new disposable probe cover per measurement. IR thermometer set in unadjusted mode per 5.8.2.2.

EMC test for non-continuous reading devices (6.4.2.4): IR thermometers not capable of producing continuous temperature readings shall have their circuitry modified to allow for continuous monitoring of IR and reference temperature signals. The peak excursions of the monitored IR and reference temperature signals measured during frequency sweep interval shall be recalculated to represent the corresponding temperature excursions. On request, the manufacturer shall make available the method of the circuit modification.

In order that purchasers may identify products conforming to requirements of this specification, producers and distributors may include a statement of compliance in conjunction with their name and address on product labels or associated printed materials, or both, such as invoices, sales literature, and the like. The following statement is suggested: 'This infrared thermometer meets requirements established in ASTM Standard (E1965-98). Full responsibility for the conformance of this product to the standard is assumed by (name and address of producer or distributor).' In the event one or more provisions of this standard are not met, a cautionary statement shall be included.

The instruction manual shall contain adequate instructions for use with sufficient detail for training in the operation, application, care, and biological and physical cleaning of the instrument and accessories. The instruction manual shall include warnings if performance of the instrument may be adversely affected should one or more of specified conditions occur (operation outside subject temperature range, operation outside operating temperature and humidity ranges, storage outside ambient temperature and humidity ranges, mechanical shock, soiled or damaged infrared optical components, absent/defective/soiled probe cover, use of unspecified probe covers).

ASTM laboratory accuracy requirements in the display range of 37 to 39 °C (98 to 102 °F) for IR thermometers is ± 0.2 °C (±0.4 °F), whereas for mercury-in-glass and electronic thermometers, the requirement per ASTM Standards E667-86 and E1112-86 is ± 0.1 °C (±0.2 °F).
Section 8 Keywords: auditory canal; body temperature; ear; fever; infrared; medical instrument; temperature; thermometer; tympanic

Instruction manual shall inform user of anticipated error sources associated with disposable or reusable probe covers and sleeves, operators' technique, anatomical variations, earwax buildups, subject cooperation when comparing IR thermometers to contact thermometers.

Environmental temperature and humidity combination test method: At each blackbody temperature, the tests shall be repeated under the ambient conditions stated in Table 1. Conditions tested include: 25°C/50%RH, 39.5°C/20%RH, 39.5°C/85%RH. Measurement data at blackbody temperature ~42°C showed max delta of 0.1°C across all conditions.

Individual measurement error formula used throughout all test tables: δj = |tj - tBB|, where tj = displayed or calculated value of unadjusted temperature, tBB = true temperature of the blackbody, j = sequential number of a reading, | | = signifies taking an absolute value. The largest δj is a measure of the laboratory error of a system.

Reference temperature source total uncertainty is consistently 0.06°C across all test conditions (Shock, Storage Conditions, Cleaning and Disinfection, Electrostatic Discharge, Low Power Supply Operation).

Individual measurement error formula: δ = |tj - tBB|, where tj is the displayed or calculated value of unadjusted temperature, tBB is the true temperature of the blackbody, j is the sequential number of a reading, and || signifies taking an absolute value. The largest δj is a measure of the laboratory error of a system. At blackbody setting temperature of 37°C and power supply voltage of 2.5V, the measured readings were 36.90, 36.7, 36.8, 36.9, 36.8°C with an average of 36.8°C and maximum error δ = 0.1°C.

requirements.title: General applicability
requirements.description: The following requirements shall apply to any IR thermometer that is labeled to meet these specifications.

requirements.title: Ear canal IR thermometer displayed temperature range
requirements.description: In any display mode, an ear canal IR thermometer shall display a subject's temperature over a minimum range of 34.4 to 42.2 °C (94.0 to 108.0 °F).

requirements.title: Skin IR thermometer displayed temperature range
requirements.description: A skin IR thermometer shall display a subject's temperature over a minimum range of 22 to 40.0 °C (71.6 to 104.0 °F).

requirements.title: Maximum Permissible Laboratory Error (Ear Canal IR Thermometer)
Laboratory error δ within manufacturer's specified operating ambient conditions
requirements.description: Within the manufacturer's specified operating ambient conditions (see 5.6), laboratory error δ as measured according to 6.1.4 shall be no greater than values specified below.

requirements.title: Ear canal blackbody temperature range 36 to 39 °C
requirements.description: For blackbody temperature range from 36 to 39 °C (96.8 to 102.2 °F): 0.2 °C (0.4 °F).

requirements.title: Ear canal blackbody temperature outside 36-39 °C
requirements.description: For blackbody temperatures less than 36 °C (96.8 °F) or greater than 39 °C (102.2 °F): 0.3 °C (0.5 °F).

requirements.title: Maximum Permissible Laboratory Error (Skin IR Thermometer)
Skin IR thermometer laboratory error δ
requirements.description: Within the manufacturer's specified operating ambient conditions (see 5.6) over the display temperature range as specified in 5.2.2, laboratory error δ as measured according to 6.1.5 shall be no greater than 0.3 °C (0.5 °F).

requirements.title: Clinical accuracy applicability
requirements.description: The clinical accuracy requirement is applicable only to an ear canal IR thermometer system and the corresponding age groups of subjects for which such a thermometer is labeled or implied to be used.

requirements.title: Clinical accuracy determination conditions
requirements.description: Clinical accuracy shall be determined separately for each of the following conditions: for each device model, for each adjusted display mode, and for every age group of febrile and afebrile subjects on which the IR thermometer is intended to be used.
requirements.result_remark: Clinical accuracy is not evaluated in this report.

requirements.title: Clinical accuracy disclosure
requirements.description: Any disclosure of clinical accuracy claims shall be accompanied by disclosure of methodology and procedures. Such information shall be made available on request.

requirements.title: Clinical accuracy form
requirements.description: Clinical accuracy should be determined in the form of two characteristics — clinical bias with stated uncertainty and clinical repeatability, as defined in 3.2.9.

requirements.title: Laboratory error at operating temperature range 16 to 40 °C
requirements.description: The system shall meet laboratory error requirements as specified in 5.3 or 5.4, or both, when operating in an environment from 16 to 40 °C (60.8 to 104.0 °F).

requirements.title: Labeling for narrower operating temperature range
requirements.description: If the operating temperature range is narrower than specified in 5.6.1.1, the device shall be clearly labeled with a cautionary statement of the maximum or minimum operating temperatures, or both.

requirements.title: Upper limit of operating temperature range
requirements.description: Under no circumstances may the upper limit of operating temperature range be less than 35 °C (95 °F).

requirements.title: Operating Humidity Range
requirements.description: The relative humidity range for the operating temperature range as specified in 5.6.1 is up to 95%, noncondensing.

requirements.title: Drop test with batteries installed
requirements.description: The instrument with batteries installed (if applicable) without a carrying (storage) casing shall withstand drops with controlled orientation of the device without degradation of accuracy as specified in 5.3 or 5.4, or both, for a blackbody temperature of or near 37 °C (98.6 °F), when tested according to 6.3.

requirements.title: Shock detection mechanism
requirements.description: If an IR thermometer does not meet the requirement of 5.6.3.1, a means of detecting and informing the user of its inoperable state, after being subjected to shock, shall be provided.

requirements.title: Storage Conditions
requirements.description: The instrument shall meet the accuracy requirements of 5.3 or 5.4, or both, after having been stored or transported, or both, at any point in an environment of -20 to +50 °C (-4 to +122 °F) and relative humidity up to 95%, noncondensing, for a period of one month. The test procedure is specified in 6.1.6.
Cleaning and Disinfection—Instrument performance shall not be degraded by using the manufacturer's recommended procedures for cleaning and disinfection provided in the instruction manual.

Electromagnetic Immunity—An IR thermometer that is intended for professional use shall meet the accuracy requirements of 5.3 or 5.4, or both, for temperature ranges of 6.3.2, during and after exposure to electromagnetic interference.
Electrostatic Discharge—An IR thermometer shall meet the accuracy requirements of 5.3 and 5.4, or both, for temperature ranges of 6.3.2, after 5 s after being subjected to electrostatic discharge.
Low Power Supply Operation—The instrument shall operate at power supply voltage lower by no less than 0.1 V than that required for indication of low power supply sign as specified by 5.8.3.
Display and Human Interface
Resolution—The resolution of a display shall be 0.1 °C (0.1 °F).
Modes
An IR thermometer shall indicate in what mode the instrument is set.
Unadjusted Mode—The unadjusted mode shall be accessible by the user either by setting the instrument into that mode directly or by a conversion technique from adjusted mode.
The adjusted mode sets an IR thermometer to represent a reference body site, such as core, oral, rectal, etc.
requirements.notes: Adjusted mode, reference body site: oral

requirements.description: Probe Covers
To provide a sanitary barrier between a subject and the probe, a probe cover that comes in contact with a subject.
A probe and a probe cover of the system shall have shape and dimensions that prevent injury to a subject of any age.
A probe cover shall not increase laboratory errors whose limits are set in 5.3.1.
Labeling and Marking (Instruments and Accessories)
Thermometer and Accessories
A thermometer shall clearly indicate the units of its temperature scale.
requirements.notes: See 'Instruction for Use' of the User's Manual

requirements.description: An IR thermometer housing shall be clearly marked with the trade name or type of the device, or both, model designation, name of the manufacturer or distributor, and lot number or serial number.

An IR thermometer intended for professional use shall be conspicuously labelled with an indication of the unadjusted or adjusted mode(s), or both, that correspond to the temperature value(s) capable of being displayed by the instrument.
Probe Covers Package

The package shall state the name and type of the enclosed products, name of the manufacturer or distributor, lot number or serial number, and expiration date (if the probe covers have limited shelf life).
The thermometer model(s) for which the covers are intended for use shall be specified on the probe cover package.
The package shall state whether the probe cover is intended for single use or multiple use.

Any probe cover handling, application, storage, or cleaning procedures which impact the ability of an IR thermometer to meet the requirements for maximum permissible laboratory error specified in 5.3 shall be stated.

The tests are not required for every produced instrument. However, each producer or distributor who represents its instruments as conforming to this specification shall utilize statistically based sampling plans that are appropriate for each particular manufacturing process, in the design qualification of the device, and shall keep such essential records as are necessary to document with a high degree of assurance its claims that all of the requirements of this specification are met.
The manufacturer shall make the sampling plans available upon request.
Laboratory Accuracy Tests

General—Laboratory accuracy tests are intended for verifying compliance of the design and construction of a particular type or model of IR thermometer with the error limitations specified in 5.3 or 5.4, or both.
Blackbody

Under laboratory conditions, an IR thermometer shall be tested against a blackbody standard. A recommended blackbody design is provided in Annex A1. The temperature of a blackbody shall be measured by the IR thermometer being tested in accordance with a procedure recommended by the manufacturer for the particular IR thermometer.
The true temperature of the blackbody shall be monitored by a contact imbedded or immersed thermometer with uncertainty no greater than ± 0.03 °C (±0.05 °F).
A manufacturer may require that an IR thermometer is tested only with a manufacturer-specified blackbody, rather than that described in Annex A1.
Ear Canal Type IR Thermometer

Tests shall be repeated for three blackbody temperatures, t_set within ±0.5 °C (±1 °F) of the following temperatures: 35, 37, and 41 °C (95, 98.6, and 105.8 °F). At each blackbody temperature, the tests shall be repeated under the ambient conditions stated in Table 1.
Prior to the measurements, the IR thermometer shall be stabilized at given conditions of ambient temperature and humidity for a minimum of 30 min or longer if so specified by the manufacturer.

At each combination of operating temperature and humidity in Table 1, at least six measurements shall be taken for each blackbody temperature. The number of readings shall be the same for all combinations. A new disposable probe cover (if applicable) must be used for each test reading. The rate and method of temperature taking shall be in compliance with the manufacturer's recommendations.
The requirements of 5.3 demand that no individual error δj exceeds the specified limits for laboratory error.

In each mode, three data sets shall be formed. Each data set is comprised of values δj obtained at the same blackbody temperature setting by pooling together values for all combinations of operating temperature and humidities obtained at that blackbody temperature. The largest δj is a measure of the laboratory error of a system.

The correction method to arrive at unadjusted temperature tj from readings in adjusted mode(s) shall be used according to the manufacturer's recommendation. Such recommendations shall be available from the manufacturer on request and provided in the service and repair manual, if any (see 7.3).
To comply with this standard, the greatest calculated error δj from all data sets measured and calculated for all display modes shall conform with requirements set forth in 5.3.
Skin Type IR Thermometer
Testing is as specified in 6.1.4 except that blackbody temperatures shall be set within ±1 °C (±2 °F) from the following temperatures: 23, 30, and 38 °C (73, 86, and 100 °F).
The greatest calculated error δj from all data sets shall conform with requirements set forth in 5.4.

Storage Test—To test compliance with storage conditions, an IR thermometer shall be maintained in an environmental chamber at temperature –20 °C (–4 °F), relative humidity below 50 %, for a period of 30 days and at 50 °C (122 °F), relative humidity no less than 75 % noncondensing, for a period of 30 days. After each exposure the IR thermometer shall be tested according to 6.3.2 and 6.3.3.

Clinical Accuracy Tests—This specification does not prescribe an actual method for determining clinical accuracy or establish specifications for values which characterize clinical accuracy. Manufacturers shall perform clinical accuracy testing in accordance with methods acceptable to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. An example of a method which may be used for this purpose is provided in X2.3.
Error limit for IR thermometer measurement accuracy (referenced in shock test error evaluation)
Alternative error limit for IR thermometer measurement accuracy (referenced in shock test error evaluation)
Requirement for IR thermometer shock/drop resistance (referenced in shock test)

Specification for unadjusted mode setting of IR thermometer
The probe of the electrostatic discharge device shall touch one of the electrically conductive parts on the device.
The level of discharge shall be 2, 4, and 6 kV.
After electrostatic discharge, the IR thermometer shall be tested according to the procedures of 6.3.2 and 6.3.3.
Documentation
Identification

Producers and distributors may include a statement of compliance in conjunction with their name and address on product labels or associated printed materials. Suggested statement: 'This infrared thermometer meets requirements established in ASTM Standard (E1965-98). Full responsibility for the conformance of this product to the standard is assumed by (name and address of producer or distributor).' In the event one or more provisions are not met, a cautionary statement shall be included.
The IR thermometer shall be identified as intended for professional or consumer use, or both, as applicable.
Instruction Manual
An instruction manual shall be provided and contain the system specifications including, but not limited to, specified items.

The instruction manual shall indicate the type and availability of a blackbody recommended for verifying laboratory or clinical accuracy, if only such type is required by the manufacturer as addressed in 6.1.3.3.

The instruction manual shall specify whether the probe cover is intended for single use or multiple use. If multiple use is allowed, cleaning instructions and criteria for determining when a probe cover should be discarded shall be specified. Cleaning instructions shall be adequate to prevent cross-contamination between patients.

The instruction manual shall inform the user of differences in the accuracy of measurements obtained with IR thermometers versus contact thermometers (mercury-in-glass and electronic thermometers). Such differences shall include description of anticipated error sources associated with disposable or reusable probe covers and sleeves, operators' technique, anatomical variations, earwax buildups, subject cooperation, etc. The instruction manual shall conspicuously include the statement: 'ASTM laboratory accuracy requirements in the display range of 37 to 39 °C (98 to 102 °F) for IR thermometers is ± 0.2 °C (±0.4 °F), whereas for mercury-in-glass and electronic thermometers, the requirement per ASTM Standards E667-86 and E1112-86 is ± 0.1 °C (±0.2 °F).'
Service and Repair Manual
A detailed service manual shall be made available if user service or repair is permitted by the manufacturer.
A service manual shall disclose values of instrumentation or combined site offsets, or both.
A service manual shall provide a method of arriving at unadjusted readings from temperatures displayed in an adjusted mode.

Accuracy Determination — A manufacturer shall make available upon request specific instructions for tests to determine the laboratory error, clinical bias, and clinical repeatability of an IR thermometer. When describing how clinical tests are performed, the manufacturer shall disclose the profile of subject groups tested, including age and febrile status. A detailed procedure for taking reference temperatures also shall be disclosed.
